insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's protocol confirms purchases via cryptographic receipt verification — 107,549 receipts totaling $5.1M cumulative GMV — replacing the inferential logic of cookie-based targeting with deterministic proof of transaction. For brands paying $5+ CPM on probabilistic signals, this represents a structurally different data asset.

insights.topic: Grocery vertical depth and brand coverage
insights.insight: Five distinct grocery brands have crossed the threshold in 14-day data — Walmart, Kroger, Costco, Publix, Whole Foods, with Trader Joe's intermittent — spanning mass-market through premium positioning across distinct consumer segments. No other category shows this brand-level resolution, making grocery the most actionable vertical for CPG and private-label targeting.

The 'Unknown' category carries an average ticket of $87.79 per receipt versus $44.27 for grocery, a 2x premium that has persisted across all observed windows. This elevated-ticket, unclassified segment likely contains high-value discretionary spend — a targeting signal worth investigating before category labels are finalized.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion reaching largest US metros
insights.insight: The New York-Newark-Jersey City metro (CBSA 35620) entered the active coverage set on 2026-11-23, bringing confirmed receipt flow from the largest US metro by population. Six new metro cells have been added across the current observation window, with coverage expanding in single-cell increments — steady diffusion rather than a launch spike.

insights.topic: Restaurants and dining as a durable category signal
insights.insight: Restaurants & Dining first appeared in category data on 2026-11-20 and now accounts for 841 receipts and $27,148 in 14-day GMV — comparable in dollar volume to department stores. The category has held across multiple cycles, confirming it as a stable signal for QSR, casual dining, and food-delivery brands evaluating verified post-transaction targeting.

insights.topic: Token velocity trend as a demand proxy
insights.insight: Token velocity has reached 0.664x week-over-week — the highest reading in the full observation window — with three consecutive heartbeats showing upward drift and acceleration holding above 1x. Velocity below 1x means throughput is not yet self-sustaining, but the directional trend is the relevant signal for brands timing entry into verified-receipt data partnerships.
